minutes.headline: Open Space Committee declined the Forest Legacy project and began reviewing town-owned parcels for lake access
minutes.summary: The committee approved the November 24 minutes with one amendment, then decided it lacked the bandwidth to join the Forest Legacy aggregation project. Most of the meeting went to reviewing town-owned parcels, mainly Lake Shirley and Stump Cove access options, and whether tax title takings were completed. Members also heard updates on Marshall Park planning and the conservation rules, and set January to April meeting dates.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee decided it lacked the bandwidth to join the Forest Legacy aggregation project; the chair will tell the watershed association.
Most of the meeting went to reviewing town-owned parcels, including Lake Shirley and Stump Cove access, and whether tax title takings were completed.
A member will contact the state Office of Fishing and Boating Access about public access at Lake Shirley.
A Marshall Park master planning request is in the capital plan; its place on the final list is unknown.
Meetings were set for Jan 19, Feb 16, Mar 16 and Apr 20 at 6:30.

why_it_matters: Forest Legacy is a federal conservation funding source that needs no town meeting appropriation, so declining it means no town land is offered for it this round.
Lake access and Marshall Park planning both depend on capital plan decisions and possible state grants, which could later reach residents as a Town Meeting vote or a funding request.
